objective: Prove that for p odd, r | p - 1 and G of class (K) with a hard pair, counting homomorphisms from pi1 of r-surgeries on knots (H1 = Z/r) to G is #P-hard under polynomial-time Turing reductions: anchor-graph isolation of sector 1 by a Vandermonde solve over disjoint unions, Bulatov-Grohe for the positive rank-at-least-two weight matrix, and the explicit construction for each pattern; with COPRIME-CLASS2-20261026-001C this is a dichotomy for closed 3-manifolds with bounded first homology (refined for bounds below r). Decide the extension to knot groups when commutators involve the trivial character.
status: Proved by CLASSK-DICHOTOMY-20261026-001C-P001: for p odd, r | p - 1 and G = N x| C_r of class (K) with a hard pair, counting homomorphisms from pi1 of r-surgeries on knots (H1 = Z/r) to G is #P-hard under polynomial-time Turing reductions (at most r oracle calls per value of a fixed Bulatov-Grohe partition function): the construction of COPRIME-CLASS2-20261026-001D section 3 realizes the gadget manifolds of all three slot patterns (supported end to end by CLASSK-DICHOTOMY-20261026-001B), the count is a positive sum of multiplicative sector partition functions (CLASSK-DICHOTOMY-20261026-001A), an anchor graph and a Vandermonde solve over disjoint unions isolate the hard sector, and Bulatov-Grohe applies to its positive weight matrix of rank at least two. With COPRIME-CLASS2-20261026-001C: a dichotomy for closed 3-manifolds with |H1| <= C (polynomial iff no subgroup G_d, d | r, d <= C, has a hard pair) and for knot groups, including commutators with the trivial character (the u-pairing is move-invariant and block-diagonal, so the knot count is a positive sum of multiplicative (k, beta) terms). Rowell's Conjecture 3.2(b) fails for every such G unless every #P function is polynomial-time computable.
title: With a hard pair, class-(K) counting is #P-hard with H1 = Z/r: the dichotomy
